lines: Rhosyn: There. Over the golden roofs. Wisp.
Rhosyn lifts Edrin's reel. The grey Kitelet circles lower.
Its call is so thin. Hum the Echo melody, {name}.
Wisp drops onto the reel. Then onto Rhosyn's arm.
Rhosyn: Hello, you. I'm his sister. I'm your person now.
The Thin Air over Gildcrest fills with ordinary wind.

feast_after: Rhosyn: Wisp pulls left. Edrin's kites always did.

lines: Rhosyn: After the feast. When the Gilt Rift is mended.
Rhosyn: Wilf told me. You stopped him. Thank you.
Rhosyn: The Span is mended. Edrin would have liked that.
Rhosyn: I brought his old reel. The string's still on it.
Rhosyn: Come to the feast in Gildcrest. Wisp circles there.

reel_after: Rhosyn: Gildcrest, at the feast. Wisp circles there.

lines: Rhosyn: The Span's still torn. Wisp won't come lower.
Rhosyn: See it? Over the cliffs. No string at all.
Rhosyn: Every dusk it comes. It never lands.
Rhosyn: My brother Edrin flew a Kitelet called Wisp.
Rhosyn: Edrin fell from the Gilt Span. Wisp flew off.
Rhosyn: Nine years ago. Kites don't last nine years.
Rhosyn: Ask the salt widows at Paleshore. They see far.

rhosyn_after: Rhosyn: Paleshore. The widows watch the sky for a living.

lines: Selma: That's no kite, love. It's a Kitelet. Gone grey.
Selma: It follows the old salt road to the Span. Daily.
Selma: Up here we call it the Thin Air. Calls that fade.
Selma: A Spirling that lost its person calls and calls.
Selma: Every lost call goes somewhere. To the Echo.
Selma: A choir of them. Grieving. Not angry. Just sad.
Selma: Racer Wilf wants to net it. For the cliff prize.

selma_after: Selma: Wilf's at Whitecairn with a net. Hurry.

lines: Selma: The flats lie while the Orrery's broken. Later.
Wilf: The grey kite? Five hundred coins, the cliff prize.
Wilf: Mum's roof leaks. Nets are cheap. Roofs aren't.
Wilf: You want it left alone? Then earn it.

wilf_after: Wilf: The grey one flies to the Span's middle. Every night.
wilf_defeat: Wilf: All right. No net. I'll fix the roof another way.
Wilf: Tell the kite-maker I'm sorry. I didn't know.
wilf_lose: Wilf: My net's ready. Come back if you're sure.

lines: Wilf: Wind's wrong. Come back once the salt flats calm.
